'''Liu Chen''' ({{lang-zh|s=陈骝|t=陳騮|p=Chén Liú}}; born February 4, 1946) is a Taiwanese-American theoretical physicist who has made original contributions to many aspects of [[plasma physics]]. He is known for the discoveries of [[Alfven wave|kinetic Alfven waves]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Hasegawa|first1=Akira|last2=Chen|first2=Liu|date=1976|title=Kinetic processes in plasma heating by resonant mode conversion of Alfvén wave|journal=The Physics of Fluids|volume=19|issue=12|pages=1924–1934|doi=10.1063/1.861427|bibcode=1976PhFl...19.1924H|osti=7258509|issn=0031-9171|url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc1447357/}}</ref> toroidal Alfven eigenmodes,<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Cheng|first1=C. Z.|last2=Chen|first2=Liu|last3=Chance|first3=M. S.|date=1985|title=High-n ideal and resistive shear Alfvén waves in tokamaks|journal=Annals of Physics|volume=161|issue=1|pages=21–47|doi=10.1016/0003-4916(85)90335-5|bibcode=1985AnPhy.161...21C|issn=0003-4916|url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc1182593/}}</ref> and energetic particle modes;<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Chen|first=Liu|date=1994|title=Theory of magnetohydrodynamic instabilities excited by energetic particles in tokamaks|journal=Physics of Plasmas|volume=1|issue=5|pages=1519–1522|doi=10.1063/1.870702|bibcode=1994PhPl....1.1519C|issn=1070-664X}}</ref> the theories of geomagnetic pulsations,<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Liu|last2=Hasegawa|first2=Akira|date=1974|title=A theory of long‐period magnetic pulsations: 1. Steady state excitation of field line resonance|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research|volume=79|issue=7|pages=1024–1032|doi=10.1029/JA079i007p01024|bibcode=1974JGR....79.1024C|issn= 2156-2202}}</ref> Alfven wave heating,<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Liu|last2=Hasegawa|first2=Akira|date=1974|title=Plasma heating by spatial resonance of Alfvén wave|journal=The Physics of Fluids|volume=17|issue=7|pages=1399–1403|doi=10.1063/1.1694904|bibcode=1974PhFl...17.1399C|issn=0031-9171}}</ref> and fishbone oscillations,<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Liu|last2=White|first2=R. B.|last3=Rosenbluth|first3=M. N.|date=1984|title=Excitation of Internal Kink Modes by Trapped Energetic Beam Ions|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=52|issue=13|pages=1112–1115|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1122|bibcode=1984PhRvL..52.1122C|issn=0031-9007|url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc1085350/}}</ref> and the first formulation of nonlinear [[Gyrokinetics|gyrokinetic equations]].<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last1=Frieman|first1=E. A.|last2=Chen|first2=Liu|date=1982|title=Nonlinear Gyrokinetic Equations for Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Waves in General Plasma Equilibrium|journal=The Physics of Fluids|volume=25|issue=3|pages=502–508|doi=10.1063/1.863762|bibcode=1982PhFl...25..502F|issn=0031-9171|url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc1095192/}}</ref> Chen retired from [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI) in 2012, assuming the title professor emeritus of physics and astronomy.

==Early life and education==
Chen was born in 1946 in [[Hangzhou]], China, to a family whose [[Ancestral home (Chinese)|ancestral home]] is in [[Yuyao]]. Chen's ancestral family name is Huang (黃). He is a descendant of the philosopher [[Huang Zongxi|Zongxi Huang]] (黃宗羲). His great-grandfather, Cheng-yi Huang (黃承乙) was the mayor of Taiwan County (now [[Taichung|Taichung City]]) during the [[Qing dynasty|Qing]] reign of the [[Guangxu Emperor]].

In 1950, after the [[Kuomintang]] defeat in the [[Chinese Civil War]], Chen left [[mainland China]] during the [[Retreat of the government of the Republic of China to Taiwan|Great Retreat]] with his mother, Shyue Yan King Chen (金學言; 1916–2006), and three siblings. They joined his father, Lee Chen (陳禮; 1913–2003), at the [[Tiu Keng Leng]] refugee camp in [[Hong Kong]], where he began his education. The Chen family then moved to [[Taiwan]] in 1951. 

After graduating from the [[Affiliated Senior High School of National Taiwan Normal University]] in 1962, Chen attended [[National Taiwan University]], earning his bachelor's degree in 1966. He then left Taiwan in 1967 to complete graduate studies in the United States. He earned a [[Master of Science]] (M.S.) from [[Washington State University|Washington State University, Pullman]], in 1969, and his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1972. His doctoral dissertation, completed under Charles K. Birdsall, was titled, "I. Heating of Magnetized Plasmas by Large-Amplitude Electric Field. II. Reduction of the Grid Effects in Simulation Plasmas."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ph.D. Dissertations {{!}} EECS at UC Berkeley |url=https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/Dissertations/Faculty/birdsall.html |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=www2.eecs.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
From 1972 to 1974, Chen did his postdoctoral research with [[Akira Hasegawa]] at the [[Bell Labs]]. They developed a theory for long-period magnetic pulsations in the [[magnetosphere]] based on resonant coupling between hydromagnetic compressional waves and transverse Alfvén continuous spectrum.<ref name=":4" /> This theory, later referred to as Chen-Hasegawa field-line-resonance model, successfully explained the observations in the Earth's magnetosphere by [[Louis J. Lanzerotti]], and has become the standard model for magnetic pulsations in the Earth's and other planetary magnetospheres. Soon, their focus turned to the charged particle heating via resonant absorption within Alfvén wave continuous spectrum.<ref name=":5" /> They discovered the Kinetic Alfvén wave,<ref name=":1" /> which resolves the logarithmic singularity of [[magnetohydrodynamic]] shear Alfvén waves and plays important roles in the heating, acceleration and transport of charged particles in solar, magnetospheric, and laboratory plasmas.

From 1974, Chen worked for 19 years at [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]] (PPPL) and [[Princeton University]], there his interest was directed to the study of [[Fusion power|fusion plasmas]]. He, in collaboration with [[Edward A. Frieman]], formulated and derived the first nonlinear [[Gyrokinetics|gyrokinetic]] equation,<ref name=":7" /> the Frieman-Chen equation named in their honor, which has played a fundamental role in the physics understanding of strongly magnetized plasmas in the last decades. With Chio-Zong Cheng and Morrell S. Chance, Chen predicted the existence of hydromagnetic Alfvén bound states in laboratory plasmas due to realistic [[Symmetry breaking|symmetry-breaking]] equilibrium conditions.<ref name=":2" /> These hydromagnetic Alfvén bound states were later observed in worldwide plasma experimental devices. Chen is also well known for his collaboration with Roscoe White and [[Marshall Rosenbluth]] in demonstrating theoretically that supra-thermal energetic particles can spontaneously excite in laboratory plasmas a unique macroscopic hydromagnetic wave, observed experimentally as “fishbones” from the magnetic signals.<ref name=":6" /> From 1986 until 1993, Chen served as the deputy head of the Theory Department at PPPL.

In 1993, Chen became a professor of Department of Physics & Astronomy at the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI). During this period, Chen discovered the existence of energetic-particle modes within the shear Alfvén wave [[continuous spectrum]] and introduced a unified theoretical framework to understand the distinctive features of different Alfvén bound states and energetic-particle continuum modes.<ref name=":3" />  Subsequently, in the past two decades, this theory was generalized by a series of papers written jointly with Fulvio Zonca, and named as the general fishbone-like dispersion relation.<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Liu|last2=Zonca|first2=F.|date=2016|title=Physics of Alfvén waves and energetic particles in burning plasmas|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=88|issue=1|pages=0150088|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.88.015008|bibcode=2016RvMP...88a5008C|issn=0034-6861|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2000, Chen and coworkers elucidated that [[drift wave]] [[turbulence]] can spontaneously generate coherent [[Zonal flow (plasma)|zonal flows]] via intensity-modulation interactions, resulting in turbulence self-regulation.<ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Liu|last2=Lin|first2=Z.|last3=White|first3=R.|date=2000|title=Excitation of zonal flow by drift waves in toroidal plasmas|journal=Physics of Plasmas|volume=7|issue=8|pages=3129–3132|doi=10.1063/1.874222|bibcode=2000PhPl....7.3129C|s2cid=119538645 |issn=1070-664X|url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc619197/}}</ref> This nonlinear process has a broad scope of applications and has been generalized to the zonal structures in charged particle [[phase space]].<ref name=":8" /> Chen retired from UCI in 2012.

Chen visited mainland China in 1975 for the first time after the normalization of US-China relationship. Chen has, throughout the years, played active roles in the development of plasma physics research as well as training next generation of plasma physicists both in mainland China and Taiwan. In 1985, Chen helped Shih-Tung Tsai and Changxuan Yu to establish the Chinese Summer School for Plasma Physics. In 2007, Chen initiated the Cross-Strait Symposium on the Fusion Energy and Plasma Science. Chen served, from 1997 to 2016, as the Founding Chairman of Foundation of Shih-Tung Tsai Award for Plasma Physics.  Chen was appointed as an Honorary Research Professor at [[Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences]], [[Beijing]], in 1990, [[Chao Kuang Piu|Visiting Kuang-Piu Chair Professor]] at [[Zhejiang University]],<ref>[http://www.zju.edu.cn/english/news/2004(10-12)/news041122.htm Dr. Chen Liu Appointed as a Kuang-piu Chair Professor of Zhejiang University]</ref> [[Hangzhou]], in 2004, and Visiting Kuo-Ting Chair Professor at [[National Central University]], [[Zhongli District|Zhongli]], Taiwan, in 2007. From 2006 to 2016, Chen served as the founding director of the Institute for Fusion Theory and Simulation (IFTS) at Zhejiang University. In 2016, Chen became the director emeritus.

Chen has also published a graduate textbook ''Waves and Instabilities in Plasmas'' (World Scientific Publication Co., 1987), and nurtured generations of graduate students and postdocs worldwide.

== Personal life ==
Chen married to Shingshah Lee (李醒夏) in August 1969. They have one son, Chen Pei-jin (陳培進).

==Honors and awards==
* 1981, [[Fellow]], American Physical Society
* 2004, [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]], from the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=Liu%20Chen&year=2004 2004 Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research Recipient - Liu Chen]</ref>
* 2008, [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]], from the [[European Physical Society]]<ref>[http://www.iop.org/EJ/article/0741-3335/50/12/120302/ppcf8_12_120302.pdf?request-id=f729444a-99f1-4705-8f2f-cc85158164dd Liu Chen: recipient of the 2008 European Physical Society Plasma Physics Division Hannes Alfv´en Prize]</ref>
* 2009, [[Fellow]], American Association for Advancement of Sciences
* 2011, [[Fellow]], American Geophysical Union
* 2012, [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]], from the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://phoenix.ps.uci.edu/chen/|title=Professor Liu Chen|website=phoenix.ps.uci.edu|access-date=2019-07-26}}</ref>
* 2019, [[Subrahmanyan Chandresekhar Prize]], from the [[Association of Asia Pacific Physical Societies]]<ref>[http://aappsbulletin.org/myboard/read.php?Board=others&id=143 The 2019 Subramanyan Chandrasekhar Prize in Plasma Physics]</ref>
* 2022, [[Academician]], [[Academia Sinica]]<ref name="Taipei Times" >{{cite web |last1=Chung |first1=Jake |title=Top research institute selects 19 new members |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2022/07/08/2003781372 |website=taipeitimes.com |publisher=Taipei Times |access-date=7 July 2022}}</ref>
* 2023, Yushan [[Fellow]], [[Ministry of Education (Taiwan)|Ministry of Education, ROC]]
* 2026, Distinguished Alumnus of [[National Taiwan University]]
